3. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations stating, inter-alia, that the defendants on 20.05.2004 filed an application under Order VII rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for rejection of the plaint holding that it is barred by limitation. 

 4. Mr. M. A. Sobhan, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division committed an error of law in not considering the fact that the questions of limitation is a mixed question of law and fact and the Artha Rin Adalat, the Court of first instance had been given the jurisdiction to decide the question of limitation by taking evidence and in such view of the matter, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law. The learned Advocate further submitted that Tk. 57,66,000.00 in three different accounts has been sanction to these respondents under 'BIKALPA Project' for establishment of Twisting industry and the said loan was rescheduled on 28.08.1991 for a period of 8½ years and pursuant to the conditions of re-schedulement, the respondents executed required charge documents with a letter of continuity making the validity of the charge documents till the loan is fully adjusted and the respondents also sought to make exemption of interest of the loan by acknowledging the liability of loan on 26.11.1997 and even the respondents by another two letters dated 12.09.2000 and dated 08.09.2003 acknowledged the liability of the loan and in such, circumstances, the acknowledgement for the liability of the loan before the expiration of the period of limitation shall take effect for fresh computation of the period of limitation and in such view of the matter the case has been filed within the period of limitation. 

 6. The High Court Division observed that in this case it is rather admitted fact that the Artha Rin Suit in question was filed beyond the statutory period of limitation. So, the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat evidently, has committed error and illegality in rejecting the petitioners application under Order VII rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint on the ground of limitation.
